chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Ibrahim ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Khalaf, from Musa ibn Ibrahim al-Marwazi, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who wakes up in the morning and he does not think of being unjust to anyone, Allah would forgive him what he had sinned'.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of waking up without thinking of injustice?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this chain linking Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) to the Prophet (PBUH), highlighting that morning mindfulness of one's own potential for injustice serves as a spiritual safeguard. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on *zill al-nafs* (self-oppression) and how avoiding the intent to wrong others purifies the heart, thereby securing Allah's forgiveness for past transgressions.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Kufi, from Ibrahim Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Khalaf, from Musa Bin Ibrahim Al Marouzy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘The one who wakes up in the morning and he does not think of being unjust to anyone, Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Forigve him what he had sinned’.
en.sarwar: 21. Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi has narrated from Ibrahim ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Khalaf from Musa ibn Ibrahim al-Marwazi from abu al-Hassan Musa (a.s.) who has said the following:
“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Whoever rises in the morning and has no intention to do injustice to anyone Allah forgives his sins.”
